newsitem.title: GERMANY: Dresden airport introduces tighter night flight rules.
newsitem.headline: Dresden airport introduces tighter night flight rules.

text.p: Dresden airport said it introduced new rules tightening restrictions on night flights from March 30.
Under the new rules agreed with the city of Dresden, very loud aircraft will be completely banned from operating at Dresden airport from 22:00 to 06:00, a Flughafen Dresden GmbH statement said.
The affected aircraft are those without noise certificates in accordance with International Civil Aviation Organisation (ICAO) standards, it added.
In addition, from 23:00 to 0:00 and from 05:00 to 06:00, only "very low-noise aircraft" such as Airbus A310 or Boeing 737 would be permitted to start or land.
Under existing rules, no scheduled flights apart from postal and medical services are permitted at Dresden airport from midnight until 5am.
Dresden airport added it would complete a two million mark programme to subsidise sound-proofing of some 140 homes close to the airport by the end of 1997.
